newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-BLEWETT CENTURY MAINTAINS AUSTRALIAN REVIVAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BLEWETT CENTURY MAINTAINS AUSTRALIAN REVIVAL.

text.p: Greg Blewett made an historic century to lead the continued transformation of Australian fortunes in the first test against England at Edgbaston on Sunday.
As Australia reached 352 for two at lunch on the fourth day, only eight runs behind, captain Mark Taylor eventually went for 129. But Blewett was impregnable.
At lunch he was 123 not out, making history by becoming the only player to score a century in each of his first three England-Australia matches.

Dismissed for 118 in the first innings after staggering to 54 for eight at one stage, the Australians continued to make merry against England's bowlers, whose removal of Taylor was their only success in the morning session.
Blewett's partnership of 194 with Taylor was easily the best for Australia in an Edgbaston test, beating the record held by Mark and Steve Waugh in 1993.

Mark Waugh was able to watch the latter stages of it from the pavilion rather than from hospital, having been discharged before play began. He was suffering only from a virus, not appendicitis as has been feared, and was available to bat when required.

The diagnosis was another sign that things were going Australia's way after they had suffered so badly in conceding a first innings lead of 360. With more showers forecast, their prospects of achieving at least a draw were looking much better.
England took the new ball right at the start of the day, but rarely beat the bat with it.

Taylor took early fours off the opening bowlers, Andy Caddick and Devon Malcolm, to maintain his renewed confidence after Saturday's century, and was then content to play a supporting role as Blewett dominated.
The South Australian scored 45 of the 71 runs made off 19 overs before off-spinner Robert Croft held a ball up in the wind, luring Taylor into giving him a return catch.
The captain departed to a standing ovation from all round the ground after making his highest test score for three years to end his slump and any debate about his leadership.
